name: Mitsukoshimae
tagline: Tokyo in 2 minutes and Otemachi in 2 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, where JR East and Tokyo Metro run 3 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 2 minutes to Otemachi, 19 minutes to Shinjuku, 21 minutes to Shibuya and 16 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 4.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.6 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 4.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.3 m to 4.9 m, a difference of 1.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 6 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 27 clinics and 18 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 同仁記念会明和病院, about 16 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 秋葉原メディカルクリニック, about 19 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station. JR Sobu Main Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line also call here. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line and Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: JR Sobu Main Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 新小岩→錦糸町, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line runs at 111%. Its busiest stretch is 渋谷→表参道, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥250,000 to ¥260,000 and 2LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. 3 lines and a wide choice of connections and plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 1LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Mitsukoshimae is ahead on how close the centre is and lower rent.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Mitsukoshimae. Nihombashi has the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Tokyo Metro Tozai Line and Toei Asakusa Line, a different set from Mitsukoshimae. To Tokyo, for instance, Nihombashi takes 7 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥15,000 more at Nihombashi. On safety, Mitsukoshimae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Kanda; for how close the centre is, Mitsukoshimae.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Mitsukoshimae. Kanda also has the JR Yamanote Line, JR Chuo Rapid Line and JR Keihin-Tohoku Line, which Mitsukoshimae does not. With more lines, Kanda is the better connected of the two. To Otemachi, for instance, Kanda takes 7 minutes longer. On safety, though, Mitsukoshimae comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: The data does not show a drawback particular to this station
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
中央通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 5 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 3 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
